topic: Seeing Space: Geometric Intuition in Linear Algebra
target_audience: Undergraduate students or advanced high school students beginning Linear Algebra

sections.title: Vectors as Physical Movements
lecture_lines: Start with a standard Cartesian coordinate system.
Think of a vector as a movement through space.
An arrow from the origin shows direction and distance.
animations: Fade in a faint white (#FFFFFF) coordinate grid on the black background.
Show a white (#FFFFFF) circle robot at the origin, then animate it moving 3 units right and 2 units up.
Draw a bold blue (#0000FF) arrow from (0,0) to (3,2) with a '[3, 2]' label in blue (#0000FF).

sections.title: The DNA of Space: Basis Vectors
lecture_lines: Every 2D vector is built from two fundamental pieces.
i-hat is a unit vector along the x-axis.
j-hat is a unit vector along the y-axis.
Combine these scaled pieces to reach any point.
These basic building blocks are called basis vectors.
animations: Show the origin with a faint white (#FFFFFF) grid in the background.
Draw a red (#FF0000) unit vector 'i-hat' from (0,0) to (1,0) along the x-axis.
Draw a green (#00FF00) unit vector 'j-hat' from (0,0) to (0,1) along the y-axis.
Scale red (#FF0000) i-hat 3x and green (#00FF00) j-hat -2x, then sum them tip-to-tail.
Flash the labels 'i-hat' (red #FF0000) and 'j-hat' (green #00FF00) to identify them as basis vectors.

sections.title: Transformation: Morphing the Grid
lecture_lines: Linear transformations warp the entire grid of space.
The origin must always stay fixed in place.
All grid lines must remain parallel and evenly spaced.
animations: Show a white (#FFFFFF) grid and smoothly warp all lines into a slanted configuration.
Highlight the origin (0,0) with a yellow (#FFFF00) dot, keeping it stationary during the warp.
Pulse the slanted white (#FFFFFF) grid lines to show they remain parallel and equidistant.

sections.title: Decoding the Matrix: Where do the Basis Vectors land?
lecture_lines: A matrix tells us where basis vectors land.
The first column shows i-hat's new position.
The second column shows j-hat's new position.
These two landing spots define the transformed space.
Numbers in the matrix now have a geometric meaning.
animations: Display a 2x2 matrix [[2, 1], [-1, 1]] with column 1 in red (#FF0000) and column 2 in green (#00FF00).
Animate a red (#FF0000) vector i-hat moving from (1,0) to land at (2,-1).
Animate a green (#00FF00) vector j-hat moving from (0,1) to land at (1,1).
Warp the white (#FFFFFF) background grid to align with these two new vector landing spots.
Highlight the matrix values while flashing the corresponding vector coordinates at their tips.

sections.title: The Determinant: Scaling the Area
lecture_lines: Determinants measure how much space is scaled.
Look at the area of a single unit square.
The transformation stretches or squishes this area.
This area scaling factor is the determinant.
A determinant of zero collapses space into a line.
animations: Fade in a white (#FFFFFF) coordinate grid on a black background.
Highlight a gold (#FFD700) 1x1 unit square with corners at (0,0) and (1,1).
Smoothly warp the grid so the gold (#FFD700) square transforms into a parallelogram.
Label the area of the gold (#FFD700) parallelogram as the 'determinant' value.
Flatten the entire grid into a single line and flash the determinant as '0'.
